prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow is 4.8% of the market value, a solid cash return. Also in its favour: return on capital employed is 18.6%, a strong return on the money in the business; profit grew 16.1% a year on average over three years; and profit grew 38% compared with a year earlier. Other areas on this side: growth, the balance sheet, what the price asks for the earnings.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on the recent price trend: the share price is 14.6% lower than a year ago. Also against it: over the past year the share did 12.9 percentage points worse than the Nifty 50; the share price is 30% below its 52-week high; and the 3-year maximum drawdown was -68.5%, a deep fall. Other areas on this side: price behaviour, risk.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 9 points in favour and 6 against give more points in favour. The pool score is 55 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Hold with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
